subtype: Stage 3: The target's confusion and shame [Receiver]
passage: Class teacher's note, 3B, Wednesday. Baljeet has gone to the sick room with a stomach ache four mornings out of five this week, always before first period, never after lunch. Today I kept him back while the others went to PT and asked, "Is something at school making you feel bad?" He stared at his shoes and whispered, "Harish and his friends say I smell. It's my fault, I didn't bathe properly." He begged me not to tell his parents: "Papa will come and shout and it'll get worse." I told him it was not his fault, that he was right to tell me, and that I would help keep him safe. I informed the school counsellor, Mrs Anand, before the end of the day, and together we phoned his parents this evening to plan a calm meeting tomorrow.

qa.q: How many mornings did Baljeet go to the sick room this week?
qa.a: Four mornings out of five, always before first period.

qa.q: Why did Baljeet beg the teacher not to tell his parents?
qa.a: He felt ashamed, believing the bullying was his own fault, and afraid that Papa would shout and make it worse.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that helped at this stage?
qa.a: The teacher listened, said it was not Baljeet's fault, told the counsellor the same day and phoned his parents that evening to plan a calm meeting.

qa.q: How might Baljeet's parents feel after the phone call?
qa.a: They are likely upset to learn what has been happening, but perhaps relieved to understand the stomach aches and to have a plan.

grounding: Shows a child with stomach aches before school who believes the bullying is his fault and hides it from his parents, and a teacher acting the same day.

passage:
Tuesday
At recess Deepak's gang took Kalyani's tiffin again and passed it around over her head. Kalyani didn't cry. She just stood there with empty hands. I felt sick. Ruchi laughed, but I think she only laughed so they wouldn't pick her next. Imran even threw it once. The rest of us just watched. I kept waiting for someone else to do something, Pooja who is brave, or the monitor, but everyone was waiting too. Twenty kind kids, doing nothing.
At dinner I told Ammi. She put down her spoon and listened to all of it. She said I was right to tell her, and she wrote to Kalyani's class teacher before I went to bed.
I'm still ashamed I did nothing at recess.
Sabina

qa.q: What did Deepak's gang do with Kalyani's tiffin?
qa.a: They took it and passed it around over her head.

qa.q: What was Sabina feeling while watching at recess?
qa.a: Sabina felt sick and ashamed, wanting someone to act but frozen, waiting like everyone else.

qa.q: What could one child in that crowd have done?
qa.a: One child could have stood beside Kalyani and said 'give it back', or gone straight to a teacher, instead of waiting for someone braver.

qa.q: What is it like for Kalyani when the whole crowd just watches?
qa.a: Kalyani probably feels alone and humiliated, standing with empty hands while nobody helps.

grounding: Shows classmates who feel sorry for a bullied girl yet laugh, join in or wait for someone else, so a group of kind children still allows harm.

subtype: Stage 5: An ally breaks the silence [Response]
passage: Teacher's note, Class 4A, Friday. At lunch break I noticed Shalini sitting alone on the steps again, as she has most days since some Class 6 girls started calling her names. Today Urmila walked over, sat beside her and said, loud enough for others to hear, "Come play with us. We need one more for kho-kho." Shalini hesitated, then went. Within minutes two more girls had joined their game. After the bell Urmila came to my desk, twisting her plait. "Ma'am, I'm not telling tales, but the Class 6 girls are mean to Shalini every day." I told her this was not tale-telling; it was brave and right. I spoke gently with Shalini that afternoon and, before leaving, reported it to our safeguarding lead and to her parents.

qa.q: What game did Urmila invite Shalini to play?
qa.a: Kho-kho; they needed one more.

qa.q: How was Urmila feeling when she came to the teacher's desk?
qa.a: Urmila seemed nervous, twisting her plait and worried it might look like tale-telling, yet brave enough to speak.

qa.q: Why did Urmila's two actions together make a difference?
qa.a: Sitting with Shalini changed the group's mood at once, and telling the teacher brought in an adult who could stop the older girls.

qa.q: What was it like for Shalini when Urmila sat beside her?
qa.a: Shalini probably felt surprised and hesitant at first, then relieved and included as she joined the game.

grounding: Shows a child sitting beside a bullied classmate, inviting her to play and telling a teacher afterwards, and how that shifts the group's mood.

subtype: Stage 6: Adults act on both sides [Response]
passage: Counsellor's note, Monday. After last week's report about Kunal pushing Joseph off the swings and taking his snacks, we met both families today. For Joseph: a buddy at break, a teacher on duty near the swings, and a daily check-in with me for two weeks. He smiled a little when he heard he could come to my room any time. For Kunal: he will lose break-time privileges for a week and write an apology in his own words. But I also asked him, alone, "What's been hard lately?" He was silent for a long time. Then: "Nobody at home listens. Here, when I push, everyone looks." I have set up weekly sessions with him and a meeting with his father on Thursday. He needs a consequence and a better way to be seen.

qa.q: What will Kunal lose for a week?
qa.a: He will lose break-time privileges for a week.

qa.q: What does Kunal's answer 'when I push, everyone looks' suggest he feels?
qa.a: He seems lonely and unheard at home, and pushing others makes him feel seen and powerful at school.

qa.q: Why is it wise for the school to act on both sides?
qa.a: Joseph needs protection and daily check-ins to feel safe, while Kunal needs a consequence plus support to find better ways of getting attention.

qa.q: How might Joseph feel hearing about the buddy and the daily check-ins?
qa.a: Joseph probably feels safer and a little relieved, as his small smile at being told he can come any time suggests.

grounding: Shows a school protecting a bullied child, giving the child who bullied a firm consequence, and asking what need drives him.

subtype: Stage 1: Status and a group's approval [Actor]
passage:
Monday, 10 p.m.
Today in bio, Sharmila answered a question with her usual long, careful speech, and I did her voice under my breath: "Excuse me, ma'am, technically..." Aditi snorted. Then Kiran, then the whole back row. Even Zara from the top table turned round and grinned at me. That grin. I've wanted that table to notice me since Class 8.
At lunch they saved me a seat. Someone said, "Noor, do the Sharmila voice again," so I did, and they laughed even harder. Sharmila was two tables away. I saw her put her sandwich down and stop eating. I felt a tiny pinch. But mostly I felt like I had finally got in.
I'll probably do it again tomorrow. Is that bad? It doesn't feel bad while they're laughing.

qa.q: What did Noor do in bio class?
qa.a: Noor did Sharmila's voice under the breath: "Excuse me, ma'am, technically..."

qa.q: What was Noor feeling when the top table saved a seat at lunch?
qa.a: Noor felt thrilled and accepted, as if finally let in, and that approval outweighed the tiny pinch of guilt.

qa.q: What turning point is open to Noor before tomorrow?
qa.a: Noor could take that pinch seriously, remember Sharmila putting the sandwich down, and look for ways to belong that don't cost someone else.

qa.q: What is Sharmila experiencing two tables away?
qa.a: Sharmila seems hurt and humiliated, putting her sandwich down and not eating while the table laughs at her voice.

grounding: Shows a teen hungry for status finding that mocking a classmate wins the group's laughter, a reward that outweighs the target's visible pain.

passage: The monsoon had shut the school in Gangtok for three days, and Pema was bored. Stuck at home with patchy data and nothing but her phone, she opened the photo from the class trip: Avni mid-sneeze, eyes squeezed shut. A few taps and it had pig ears and a caption. She sent it to the girls' group. "STOP I can't breathe," someone replied. By the second rainy day Pema had set up a joke account in Avni's name, posting silly "thoughts", and the group was planning a sleepover for when school reopened, with everyone invited except Avni. From behind the screen it felt like a game, like doodling on a poster. Pema never saw Avni's face when the notifications arrived. She only saw the laughing replies, the rain on the window, and the follower count creeping up.

qa.q: Why was the school in Gangtok shut?
qa.a: The monsoon had shut the school for three days.

qa.q: Why did the cruelty feel so light to Pema?
qa.a: From behind the screen it felt like a harmless game; Pema was bored and pleased by the laughing replies, and never saw Avni's hurt.

qa.q: What could someone in the girls' group do at this stage?
qa.a: Someone could refuse to share the photo, report the fake account, tell a teacher or parent, and message Avni privately so she is not alone.

qa.q: What is Avni likely experiencing as the notifications arrive?
qa.a: Avni is probably humiliated and frightened, seeing her face mocked, her name used by a fake account and herself shut out of the sleepover.

grounding: Shows mockery escalating to an edited photo, a fake account and exclusion, with the screen making cruelty feel light to the sender.

passage:
Gautam: you weren't at lunch again
Naveen: wasn't hungry
Gautam: you ate alone on the stairs. I saw
Naveen: it's fine
Gautam: you haven't said one word in class all week
Naveen: nothing to say
Gautam: is it the video thing? the one they keep sharing?
Naveen: ...
Naveen: every time I walk in someone plays the sound
Naveen: I can't sleep. I keep hearing it
Naveen: don't tell anyone. nobody would believe me anyway, they'd say it's just jokes
Gautam: I believe you. and I'm not keeping this secret, sorry. my dad's right here. can he call your mum now?
Naveen: ...ok
Twenty minutes later Gautam's father was on the phone with Naveen's mother. By eight o'clock she had emailed the class teacher and was sitting beside Naveen on the bed, listening.

qa.q: What happens every time Naveen walks into class?
qa.a: Someone plays the sound from the video.

qa.q: Why does Naveen keep saying 'it's fine'?
qa.a: Naveen feels ashamed and hopeless, believing nobody would believe it and that it would be brushed off as jokes.

qa.q: What did Gautam do that helped, and why was it right?
qa.a: Gautam said 'I believe you', refused to keep it secret and got a parent to call Naveen's mother that same evening, so an adult could act.

qa.q: What is it like for Gautam to go against Naveen's wish for secrecy?
qa.a: Gautam may feel torn and worried about upsetting a friend, but chooses safety over secrecy because Naveen is clearly suffering.

grounding: Shows a bullied teen who stops speaking, eats alone and sleeps badly while saying it is fine, and a friend bringing in adults the same evening.

passage:
Monday. When the edited photo of Farida flashed on Kunal's phone in the corridor, Shreya laughed. Just once, a short surprised laugh. Farida was standing right there. That night Shreya lay awake replaying Farida's face.
Wednesday. The photo arrived on Shreya's phone with "fwd to everyone lol". Her thumb hovered. If she didn't forward it, would they notice? Would she be next? She deleted it without sending. Her heart pounded as if she had done something huge.
The following Monday. Shreya messaged Farida privately: "I'm sorry I laughed last week. It wasn't funny. I deleted the photo. Want to sit together at lunch?" Farida replied, "thank you. yes." After school Shreya showed Ms Iyer the forward chain. Ms Iyer thanked her, kept her name out of it, and phoned Farida's parents that evening.

qa.q: What did Shreya do with the forwarded photo on Wednesday?
qa.a: She deleted it without sending.

qa.q: How did Shreya feel that Monday night after laughing?
qa.a: She felt guilty, lying awake and replaying Farida's face.

qa.q: Which of Shreya's small acts helped, even without confronting anyone in public?
qa.a: Deleting the photo instead of forwarding it, apologising privately to Farida, inviting her to lunch and showing a teacher the chain.

qa.q: What might Farida feel reading Shreya's private message?
qa.a: Farida is likely relieved and a little less alone, since someone who laughed has apologised and offered to sit with her.

grounding: Shows a classmate torn between guilt for laughing once and fear of being targeted, choosing quiet support like a private message and refusing to forward.

passage:
"Pradeep Sir, can I show you something?" Parul held out her phone. "I saved everything. Twenty-three screenshots, with dates."
"Sit down, Parul. Take your time."
"It's the Class 10 group. They made a page about me. My mum said I should bring these to you."
He scrolled slowly, not smiling, not rushing. "You did exactly the right thing, saving these and telling us. That isn't weakness. It's how we protect you."
"Will they know I told? Will I have to change sections?"
"No. You're not the one who moves. And your phone stays yours. I'll speak to the principal today, and the students responsible will be dealt with under the school rules."
"And if it gets worse after?"
"Then you come straight back here, any day. I'll also call your mum this afternoon so she knows what we're doing."
Parul let out a long breath. "Okay."

qa.q: How many screenshots had Parul saved?
qa.a: Twenty-three screenshots, with dates.

qa.q: What was Parul worried about as she showed the screenshots?
qa.a: She was anxious that the others would know she had told, and afraid she might be the one made to change sections.

qa.q: How did Pradeep Sir make sure Parul did not pay for speaking up?
qa.a: He said she would not move sections and her phone stays hers, that the students responsible would face the school rules, and that he would call her mum that afternoon.

qa.q: How might Parul's mum feel when Pradeep Sir calls?
qa.a: She would likely feel relieved and reassured that her advice was right and that the school is acting seriously.

grounding: Shows a teen saving screenshots and reporting bullying to a counsellor who takes it seriously and acts without making her pay for speaking.

passage: Counsellor's note, end of term. Six weeks since the incidents involving Ramesh and Lokesh in Class 9. Ramesh served his suspension and has attended five of six sessions with me. Early on he shrugged: "It was just a joke." Two weeks ago I read him, without names, what Lokesh had written about lying awake before school. Ramesh went very quiet and asked if he could write to Lokesh. He also spoke for the first time about the pressure at home to be "the strong one". Lokesh has been meeting me weekly as well. Last Friday he presented his science model to the whole class, his voice shaking at first, then steady. In yesterday's class circle, several students admitted they had seen it and said nothing. One girl said, "Next time I won't just watch." I will keep both boys' check-ins going next term.

qa.q: How many sessions has Ramesh attended?
qa.a: Ramesh has attended five of six sessions.

qa.q: What does Ramesh going quiet after hearing Lokesh's words suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he finally felt the weight of the harm, perhaps ashamed or remorseful, since he then asked to write to Lokesh.

qa.q: What made this repair more than just punishment?
qa.a: Ramesh got a consequence plus sessions to understand the harm and his own pressure at home, Lokesh got weekly support, and the class reflected on staying silent.

qa.q: How might Lokesh have felt presenting the science model to the class?
qa.a: Lokesh was probably nervous at first, with a shaking voice, then steadier and likely proud as his confidence returned.

grounding: Shows a student who bullied facing consequences and a chance to understand the harm, the target regaining confidence, and bystanders learning that silence has a cost.
